newsitem.title: USA: Hilton holders approve Bally deal.
newsitem.headline: Hilton holders approve Bally deal.

text.p: Hilton Hotels Corp Thursday said its shareholders overwhelmingly approved the company's acquisition of Bally Entertainment Corp at a special meeting in Beverly Hills.
In a statement, Hilton said the $3.0 billion acquisition, which includes assumption of debt, would make Hilton the world's largest gaming company.
The transaction, which is still subject to regulatory approvals, is expected to close by November or December.

Hilton President and Chief Executive Stephen Bollenbach, also named Bally Entertainment Chairman and Chief Executive Arthur Goldberg to the post of executive vice president for Hilton Hotels and president of its gaming operations.

Goldberg's new position, which becomes effective immediately after completion of the acquisition, means he will have overall management responsibility for the combined Hilton-Bally gaming operation. That currently is comprised of 16 casinos with a total of more than 800,000 square feet of gaming space.
Goldberg will also join the Hilton board of directors.

Separately, Hilton said shareholders approved the company's previously announced 4-for-1 stock split. The record date for the split is September 19, and the mail date for the additional shares is September 25.
In addition, Hilton said its board of directors intended to increase the dividend on post-split common shares by 6.7 percent to $0.08 a share. The increase is expected to take effect in December.
The board also authorized the company to buy up to five million shares of its common stock on a pre-split basis should market conditions make such purchases attractive.
Under the authorization, the company said it may also purchase common stock to be used to fund certain employee stock compensation plans.
Bally shareholders approved the deal Wednesday.
Hilton stock rose 1-3/8 to 107 at 1500 EDT/1900 GMT Thursday, while Bally was up 1/8 at 26-7/8.
